farraa:1-1.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿قۤ وَٱلْقُرْآنِ ٱلْمَجِيدِ﴾.
Qāf: in it is the meaning by which He swore [181/b]. It is reported that it means "it has been decreed (quḍiya), by Allah", as is said of ḥumma: "it has been decreed, by Allah"; "ḥumma, by Allah" means: it has been decreed.
And it is said that (Qāf) is a mountain surrounding the earth. If it is so, it is as though it is in the position of the nominative, i.e. "it is Qāf, by Allah"; and it [should] have shown its nominative ending, because it would be a noun and not a spelled letter. Perhaps the qāf alone was mentioned from its name, as the poet said:
قلنا لها: قفى، فقالت: قافْ
(We said to her: "Stop!" and she said: "Qāf.")
She mentioned the qāf, meaning the qāf of wuqūf (stopping), i.e. "I am stopping."

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying: ﴿أَإِذَا مِتْنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَاباً﴾.
Speech before which there appears nothing to which this would be an answer; but its meaning is implied. It was only, and Allah knows best: ﴿ق وَالْقُرْآنِ الْمَجِيدِ﴾ "you will surely be raised" after death. So they said: "Shall we be raised when we have become dust?", denying the resurrection; then they said: ﴿ذَلِكَ رَجْعُ بَعِيدٌ﴾, denying it altogether. [And] His saying (بعيد) is as you say to a man who errs in a question: "You have gone a way far from the right", i.e. you have erred.

farraa:4-6.t:
His saying: ﴿قَدْ عَلِمْنَا مَا تَنقُصُ ٱلأَرْضُ مِنْهُمْ﴾: what it consumes of them.
His saying: ﴿فِيۤ أَمْرٍ مَّرِيجٍ﴾.
In error.
His saying: ﴿وَمَا لَهَا مِن فُرُوجٍ﴾.
There is no gap or crack in it.

farraa:9-9.t:
His saying: ﴿وَحَبَّ ٱلْحَصِيدِ﴾.
The grain is the harvested; and it is among what is annexed to itself, like His saying: ﴿إِنَّ هَذا لَهُو حَقُّ الْيَقِين﴾; and like it: ﴿وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ الْوَرِيدِ﴾.
The ḥabl (rope) is the warīd (jugular vein) itself, annexed to itself because the wording of its two names differs. Al-warīd is a vein between the throat and the two neck-tendons (ʿilbāwān).

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلنَّخْلَ بَاسِقَاتٍ﴾.
Tall. One says: "it has grown (basaqa) in height"; so they are the tall palms.
His saying: ﴿لَّهَا طَلْعٌ نَّضِيدٌ﴾.
He means: the palm spathe (kufurrā) while it is in its sheaths, it is naḍīd, i.e. arranged one part over another; when it comes out of its sheaths it is not naḍīd.

farraa:15-15.t:
His saying: ﴿أَفَعَيِينَا بِٱلْخَلْقِ ٱلأَوَّلِ﴾.
He says: how, in their view, should We be wearied by the resurrection when We were not wearied by creating them the first time? Then He said: ﴿بَلْ هُمْ فِي لَبْسٍ مِّنْ خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ﴾, i.e. they are in error and doubt.

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلإِنسَانَ وَنَعْلَمُ مَا تُوَسْوِسُ بِهِ نَفْسُهُ﴾.
The hāʾ is for ما; and in ما توسوس you may make the hāʾ for the man whom it whispers to, meaning: it whispers to him and talks to him.

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿عَنِ ٱلْيَمِينِ وَعَنِ ٱلشِّمَالِ قَعِيدٌ﴾.
It says قعيد and does not say قعيدان (dual). Al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: and Ḥibbān ibn ʿAlī narrated to me, from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "seated (qaʿīd) on the right and on the left" means seated ones (quʿūd); so he made qaʿīd a plural, as you make al-rasūl (messenger) for a group and for two. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿إِنَّا رَسُولُ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِين﴾, of Moses and his brother. And the poet said:
ألِكْنى إليها، وخيرُ الرسو * لِ أعلَمُهم بنواحِى الْخَبَرْ
(Be my messenger to her; and the best of messengers is the one most knowing of the sides of the news.)
So he made al-rasūl for the plural. This is one view. And if you wish, you make al-qaʿīd singular, one being sufficient for its companion, as the poet said:
نَحْنُ بما عِندنا، وأنت بما * عندك راضٍ، والرأىُ مختلِفُ
(We with what we have, and you with what you have, are content [rāḍin, singular]; and opinion differs.)
And like it is the saying of al-Farazdaq:
إِنِّى ضَمِنت لمن أتانى ما جَنَى * وأبَى، وَكان وكنت غير غَدُورِ
(I guaranteed to whoever came to me [protection from] what he had committed, and my father [did likewise]; and he was, and I was, not treacherous [ghadūr, singular].)
And he did not say غدورين (dual).

farraa:19-19.t: His saying: ﴿وَجَاءَتْ سَكْرَةُ الْمَوْتِ بِالْحَقِّ﴾. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: سكرة الحق بالموت. If you wish, you mean by (بالحق) that He is Allah, Mighty and Majestic; and if you wish, you make the stupor (al-sakra) the death itself, annexed to itself, as though you said: "the true stupor came with death". And His saying: ﴿سَكْرَةُ الْمَوْتِ بِالْحَقِّ﴾: he says: with the truth which had not been clear to them of the matter of the Hereafter. And the truth may be the death, i.e. the stupor of death came with the reality of death.

farraa:22-22.t:
His saying: ﴿فَبَصَرُكَ ٱلْيَوْمَ حَدِيدٌ﴾.
He says: you used to deny, but today you are knowing, of piercing sight; and sight here is knowledge, not with the eye.

farraa:23-23.t:
His saying: ﴿هَـٰذَا مَا لَدَيَّ عَتِيدٌ﴾.
You put عتيد in the nominative by making it a predicate whose ṣila (relative clause) belongs to ما; and if you wish, you make it resumptive (mustaʾnaf), like His saying: ﴿هَذَا بَعْلِى شَيْخٌ﴾. Had it been accusative, it would have been correct, because هذا and ما are both definite, so العتيد is detached (yuqṭaʿ) from them [as a ḥāl].

farraa:24-24.t:
[182/a] His saying: ﴿أَلْقِيَا فِي جَهَنَّمَ كُلَّ كَفَّارٍ عَنِيدٍ﴾.
The Arabs command the one and the group with what two are commanded, saying to a man: "Get up (قوما, dual) away from us". I heard one of them [say]: "Woe to you! Saddle her (ارحلاها, dual) and drive her (ازجرها, singular)". And one of them recited to me:
فقلت لصاحبى لا تحبسانا * بنزع أصوله، واجتزَّ شيحا
(I said to my companion: "Do not detain us [dual] by pulling up its roots, and cut [singular] some wormwood.")
He said: and it is also transmitted: واجدزّ, meaning واجتز. He said: and Abū Tharwān recited to me:
وإن تزجرانى يا ابن عفان أنزجر * وإن تدعانى أَحْمِ عرضاً ممنَّعاً
(If you two [i.e. you] restrain me, O son of ʿAffān, I am restrained; and if you two leave me, I will defend an honour that is well guarded.)
We think this comes from them because the fewest helpers a man has with his camels and sheep are two; and likewise a travelling company, the fewest they are is three; so the speech to one ran as speech to his two companions. Do you not see that the poets most often say: "O my two companions, O my two friends"? Imruʾ al-Qays said:
خليلىّ، مرّا بِى على أم جندب * نُقضِّى لُبانات الفؤاد المعذب
(My two friends, pass with me by Umm Jundab, that we may fulfil the needs of the tormented heart.)
Then he said:
ألَمْ تَرَ أنى كلما جئت طارقا * وجدت بها طيبا وإن لم تطيب
(Have you [singular] not seen that whenever I came by night, I found fragrance with her, even when she was not perfumed?)
So he said ألم تر, returning to the singular, while the beginning of his speech was to two. He said: and another recited to me:
خليلىّ قوما فى عَطالة فانظرا * أناراً ترى من نحو بابَيْن أو برقا
(My two friends, stand on ʿAṭāla and look: do you [singular] see a fire towards Bābayn, or lightning?)
And some of them [recite]: أنارا نرى.
His saying: ﴿مَا أَطْغَيْتُهُ﴾: the angel who used to write down the evil deeds of the unbeliever says it. That is because the unbeliever said: "He used to hurry me away from repentance"; so he said: "I did not make him transgress, O Lord, but he was astray."

farraa:29-29.t: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿مَا يُبَدَّلُ ٱلْقَوْلُ لَدَيَّ﴾, i.e. no lie is told before Me, because of His knowledge, Mighty and Majestic, of the unseen of that.

farraa:32-33.t:
His saying: ﴿هَـٰذَا مَا تُوعَدُونَ لِكُلِّ أَوَّابٍ حَفِيظٍ﴾ ﴿مَّنْ خَشِيَ﴾.
If you wish, you make (مَن) genitive, following His saying (لكلّ); and if you wish, you make it resumptive, so it is nominative, with the conditional (jazāʾ) meaning intended: whoever fears the All-Merciful in the unseen, it will be said to him: "Enter Paradise". And (ادْخُلوها) is the apodosis (jawāb) of the condition, before which you have implied the verb of saying, and you made it a verb for the plural because مَن may have the sense of the plural.

farraa:36-36.t:
His saying: ﴿فَنَقَّبُواْ فِي ٱلْبِلاَدِ﴾.
The reading of the readers. He says: they pierced through the lands and travelled in them; so was there for them any escape from death? You imply كان here, as He said: ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِّنْ قَرْيَةٍ هي أَشَدُّ قُوّةً مِّنْ قَرْيَتِكَ الَّتى أَخْرَجَتْكَ أَهْلَكْنَاهُمْ فَلا نَاصِرَ لَهُم﴾, and the meaning is: they had no helper when they were destroyed. And whoever reads: (فَنقِّبوا) فى البلاد, with kasra on the qāf, it is like a threat, i.e. go about in the lands, come and go.

farraa:37-37.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَذِكْرَىٰ لِمَن كَانَ لَهُ قَلْبٌ﴾.
He says: for whoever has intellect. This is allowed in Arabic: you say "You have no heart", "Your heart is not with you" and "Where has your heart gone?", meaning the intellect in all of that.
His saying: ﴿أَوْ أَلْقَى ٱلسَّمْعَ﴾.
He says: or he lends his hearing to the Book of Allah while he is shahīd, i.e. present, not absent.

farraa:38-38.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَا مَسَّنَا مِن لُّغُوبٍ﴾.
He says: of weariness. That is because the Jews of the people of Medina said: He began the creation of the heavens and the earth on Sunday and finished on Friday, and rested on the Sabbath. So Allah sent down: ﴿وَمَا مَسَّنَا مِن لُّغُوبٍ﴾, belying their saying. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read it: من لَغوب, with fatḥa on the lām, and it is anomalous (shādhdh).

farraa:40-40.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمِنَ ٱللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْهُ وَأَدْبَارَ ٱلسُّجُودِ﴾.
And إِدبار. Whoever reads وأدبار makes it the plural of dubur: adbār; and they are the two rakʿas after the sunset prayer. That came from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, that he said: [182/b] "وأدبار السجود: the two rakʿas after the sunset prayer"; and ﴿وإِدْبارَ النُّجومِ﴾: the two rakʿas (before the dawn prayer). ʿĀṣim used to give fatḥa to the one in Qāf and kasra to the one in al-Ṭūr; giving both kasra and giving both fatḥa are allowed.

farraa:41-41.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱسْتَمِعْ يَوْمَ يُنَادِ ٱلْمُنَادِ مِن مَّكَانٍ قَرِيبٍ﴾.
It is said that Gabriel, peace be upon him, will come to Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis) and call out for the Gathering; that is His saying: ﴿مِن مَّكَانٍ قَرِيبٍ﴾.

farraa:44-44.t:
His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ تَشَقَّقُ ٱلأَرْضُ عَنْهُمْ سِرَاعاً﴾.
To the place of Gathering; and تُشَقق [is also read]; and the meaning is one, like "the man died (māta)" and "was caused to die (umīta)".

farraa:45-45.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَآ أَنتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِجَبَّارٍ﴾.
He says: you are not a dominator over them. He put al-jabbār in the position of al-sulṭān (the ruler), from al-jabriyya (compulsion). He said: al-Mufaḍḍal recited to me:
ويوم الحَزن إذ حشَدَت مَعدٌّ * وكان الناسُ إلا نحن دينا عصينا عزمةَ الجبار حتى * صبحنا الجوفَ ألفا مُعْلمينا
(And the Day of al-Ḥazn, when Maʿadd gathered and all people but us were in subjection: we defied the resolve of the jabbār until we came upon al-Jawf in the morning, a thousand men wearing battle-marks.)
By al-jabbār he meant al-Mundhir, because of his rule.
And al-Kalbī said, with his isnad: لستَ عَلَيْهِمْ بجَبّار: he says: you were not sent to compel (tajburahum) them to Islam and guidance; you were sent only as a reminder, so remind. That was before he was commanded to fight them.
The Arabs do not say faʿʿāl from afʿaltu: they do not say "this is a kharrāj" or "a dakhkhāl", meaning mudkhil and mukhrij, from adkhaltu and akhrajtu; they say only dakhkhāl from dakhaltu, and faʿʿāl from faʿaltu. The Arabs have said darrāk from adraktu, but it is anomalous. If you take al-jabbār in this sense [i.e. from ajbara], it is a valid view.
And I have heard some of the Arabs say: "jabarahu ʿalā al-amr", meaning ajbarahu (he compelled him); so al-jabbār from this dialect is sound, meaning: one who subdues them and compels them.
